summary: Add a nullable BIGINT column referrer_id_new, backfill values, deploy the new version with state_only migration, retire the old version, then clean referrer_id of any values that do not reference existing users before adding the ForeignKey constraint, completing the schema change with zero downtime.
write_consistency: During the overlap between deploy_new and retire_old the FK constraint is not yet active, so both the old and new versions can write integer values to referrer_id without referential integrity violations. After retire_old a SQL stage sets referrer_id to NULL for any rows referencing non‑existent users, after which the FK constraint is added, ensuring the new version’s writes respect the self‑reference.
revision_notes: The previous plan failed because the FK constraint was added after retire_old while referrer_id still contained values that did not exist as account_user rows, causing a foreign‑key violation. The revision adds a cleanup SQL stage after retire_old that nullifies those invalid referrer_id values before the constraint is created, satisfying the runner's checks.

stages.description: Retire the old Saleor version; after this stage only the new version serves traffic.
Set referrer_id to NULL for rows where the referenced user does not exist, then add the ForeignKey constraint.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET referrer_id = NULL WHERE referrer_id IS NOT NULL AND referrer_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM account_user);
ALTER TABLE account_user ADD CONSTRAINT fk_referrer FOREIGN KEY (referrer_id) REFERENCES account_user(id);
